grounding_notice: General Knowledge Mode: Material synthesized from foundational domain principles.

concepts.title: Inertia & Newton's First Law (The Core Truth)
concepts.explanation_focus: Why objects keep moving forever without friction, and why inertia is mass.
concepts.analogy: A frictionless skateboard gliding through deep space without ever slowing down.

checkpoint_question.question: If an astronaut throws a wrench in deep space where no friction or gravity exists, what happens?
options: The wrench eventually slows down and stops because force runs out.
The wrench continues moving forever at the same constant speed in a straight line.
The wrench orbits back to the astronaut.
The wrench instantly falls straight down.
checkpoint_question.rubric: Evaluates understanding that continuous motion does not require continuous force in the absence of net external force.

misconception_traps.0: Aristotelian misconception: Believing motion requires an ongoing push.

concepts.title: Action-Reaction Pairs (Newton's Third Law)
concepts.explanation_focus: Forces always come in mutual pairs acting on separate bodies, so they never cancel out.
concepts.analogy: Stepping off a boat onto a dock: you push the boat back, the boat pushes you forward.

checkpoint_question.question: If action and reaction forces are equal and opposite, why don't they cancel each other out?
checkpoint_question.sample_answer: They do not cancel because they act on two different objects, not on the same object.
checkpoint_question.rubric: Must explicitly identify that forces act on two distinct/different bodies.

misconception_traps.cancel: Canceling forces fallacy: Thinking action-reaction act on the identical body.
